name: Corporate statism
scope: State corporatism (the 'corporate state'): society organised into officially recognised occupational corporations or syndicates of employers and workers, subordinate to and controlled by an authoritarian state (s5, s6). The defining sources present it as practised in Mussolini's Italy (syndical confederations from 1926, the Labor Charter of 1927, the Council of Corporations of 1934-36: s5, s7) and in Salazar's Estado Novo with its Corporative Chamber and state syndicates (s8), with intellectual roots in Adam Muller's Standestaat, Othmar Spann and Catholic social teaching (s5, s6, s8). It excludes neo-corporatism or societal corporatism, the voluntary bargaining of democratic states between government, labour and business (s5, s6), which the defining sources set against it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says that a contract of hiring for wages is not unjust by its nature, and the Labor Charter regulates wage payment in collective contracts (art. 11, 14).

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says the wage contract is not unjust by its nature; the Labor Charter regulates wage contracts (arts. 11, 14).

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno defends private ownership and the Labor Charter calls private initiative the most useful instrument of production.

central-planning.rationale: Split within the texts: Schneider calls the corporate state an attempt at a national administration of production with private ownership kept, while the Labor Charter limits State intervention to where private initiative is lacking (art. 9).

class-collaboration.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno and the Labor Charter (arts. 4, 26) make collaboration of classes the principle, and Britannica describes corporatism as the way to 'socially harmonious class participation'.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Labor Charter requires collective labour contracts made by recognised syndicates to set wages and conditions (arts. 3, 11), though under State arbitration.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says free competition cannot direct economic life and is 'a poisoned spring' of individualist errors.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The defining feature: only the State-recognised syndicate may represent employers or workers and make collective contracts binding on the whole group (art. 3), with the Ministry of Corporations as final authority (s5, s7).

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Labor Charter has syndicates and courts guarantee the relation between wages and normal living costs (art. 12), and promises insurance (art. 27); Quadragesimo Anno demands a family-supporting wage.

decide-locally.rationale: Schneider shows the 1934 reform allowed only national organisations legal recognition, making provincial bodies branches of national federations under the Ministry of Corporations.

defeat-communism.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno condemns communism; Gallagher says the Constitution was firmly opposed to socialism and communism.

democracy-best.rationale: Gallagher says the 1933 Constitution embraced undemocratic politics and was meant to correct the excesses of individualism; in Italy the Council of Corporations succeeded the Chamber of Deputies (s5).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno condemns communism's class warfare and says that socialism cannot be reconciled with Christian teaching.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says mothers should work primarily in the home.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Salazar stressed reducing external dependence to a minimum (s8); Schmitter connects state corporatism with the desire for national autarky (s6).

equal-outcomes.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno wants a just distribution of goods but within classes of owners and wage earners, and calls for each class to receive its due, not equal results.

family-wage.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says the wage must suffice to support a worker and his family.

free-trade.rationale: Salazar's order subordinated all rules to the nation's superior interests and aimed to cut external dependence to a minimum, with curbs on foreign investment (s8); Schmitter ties state corporatism to a desire for national economic autarky (s6).

independent-unions.rationale: Only the State-recognised syndicate may represent workers (s9 art. 3, s7); in Portugal syndicates needed State approval and were dissolved if they diverged from the model (s8).

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Labor Charter holds that the nation is an organism with aims and life superior to those of the individuals composing it (art. 1).

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Labor Charter aims at the increase and perfection of products and national strength (arts. 2, 8); Schneider describes the system as a national administration of production.

industrial-unions.rationale: Schneider describes syndicates by occupation (categoria) grouped in national federations and confederations by industry, agriculture, commerce and credit.

informal-organisation.rationale: Only the one State-recognised association per branch may represent a group; Schneider notes de facto associations do not in practice exist.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The Labor Charter subordinates both to the interests of production and leaves direction of the enterprise to the employer (arts. 4, 7).

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno calls the claim that all products and profits belong to workers a fictitious principle and says capital and labour need each other.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says free competition 'clearly cannot direct economic life' and must be directed by the State and vocational bodies, while the Labor Charter keeps private initiative as the most useful instrument under State supervision.

more-religion-public.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno calls for the reform of institutions and customs by Christian principles; Gallagher says the papacy was the one outside influence Salazar acknowledged.

nation-first.rationale: The Labor Charter treats production as a national interest and the nation as superior to its individuals (arts. 1, 6); Salazar's rules were subordinated to 'the superior interests of the nation' (s8).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Gallagher says the corporative doctrine grew from thinkers alienated from capitalism and decried both capitalist individualism and the materialist state; the Charter keeps private initiative and Quadragesimo Anno rejects socialism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Labor Charter lets the State control, encourage or manage production (art. 9) and Salazar's state controlled life in the workplace through licensing and labour statutes (s8).

one-party-rule.rationale: In Salazar's state freedom of association did not extend to political parties and only the National Union could nominate candidates until 1945 (s8); Fascist Party chiefs sat at the head of Italy's corporative committees (s7).

organic-representation.rationale: Salazar's Corporative Chamber was staffed by functional interests (s8); Italy's council was made of employer and employee confederations (s5); the Charter treats corporations as State organs (art. 6).

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Assembly was a deliberative body that could not propose laws affecting revenue and the government could rule by decree (s8); Italy's council replaced the Chamber of Deputies (s5).

person-over-state.rationale: The Labor Charter holds that the nation is superior to the individuals who compose it (art. 1).

production-for-use.rationale: The Labor Charter keeps private initiative and the employer's direction of the enterprise (art. 7) and tells employers to reduce costs (art. 8), alongside the producers' well-being and national strength (art. 2).

profit-exploitation.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno denies the wage contract is unjust and treats capital and labour as needing each other.

property-fundamental.rationale: Split within the words: Quadragesimo Anno and the Labor Charter defend private property and private enterprise, but make them answerable to the common good and the State (s9 art. 7) so it is not an overriding right.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno holds ownership has an individual and a social character and must serve the common good.

public-ownership.rationale: The Labor Charter makes private initiative the preferred instrument and allows direct State management only where private initiative is lacking or insufficient (arts. 7, 9); the corporate state keeps private ownership of the means of production (s7).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Split within the texts: the Labor Charter drops a fixed minimum wage and says no fixed rule can be prescribed (s7), yet ties wages to normal living costs (art. 12, s9), and Quadragesimo Anno demands a wage that supports a worker and his family (s2).

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Labor Charter makes each enterprise responsible to the State for its direction of production (art. 7); Salazar's corporative order required State licences to build, extend or move a plant (s8).

restore-past-order.rationale: Split within the words: Gallagher notes the corporative ideal reaches back to medieval guilds, while Britannica says Muller sought a 'modernized' Standestaat.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The 1926 law prohibited strikes and lockouts (s7); in Portugal the right to strike was abolished (s8); Quadragesimo Anno says strikes and lock-outs are forbidden and public authority intervenes.

second-chamber.rationale: The Portuguese Corporative Chamber served as the regime's upper house alongside the National Assembly.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Labor Charter subordinates the opposing interests of employers and workers to the superior interests of production (art. 4), and treats labour as a social duty (art. 2).

separated-powers.rationale: Under the 1933 Constitution the government could legislate by decree, the Assembly was deliberative not legislative, and the prime minister's powers did not depend on its votes.

socialized-markets.rationale: The Labor Charter makes private initiative the main instrument of production (art. 7), and Quadragesimo Anno rejects socialism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Labor Charter presents the State as the organ that reconciles employer and worker interests with legal equality (arts. 4-6), and Britannica describes the system as mediating between them.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Gallagher: industrial licensing required prior State authorisation for plants and for added machinery, and credit was curbed; the Labor Charter allows control, encouragement or direct management where the State's political interests are involved (art. 9).

state-harmful.rationale: The Labor Charter holds the nation 'completely realized in the Fascist State' (art. 1), and Mussolini 'placed the state at the heart of the corporatist ideal' (s8): the state is the centre of the order, not something to abolish.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The 1933 Constitution entitled the state to prevent 'the perversion of public opinion' and 'safeguard the moral integrity of citizens'.

strong-leader.rationale: Britannica says the corporate state 'reflected the will of the country's dictator'; Gallagher says the Constitution made the prime minister the dominant figure with complete authority.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Gallagher: rebellion against the corporativist order was swiftly put down, censorship was regulated by the interior ministry and crimes against the security of the state were punished.

taxation-theft.rationale: The recognised syndicates may impose contributions on all in the group (art. 3), which Schneider calls 'practically a tax levied on all members of the national economy'.

total-state.rationale: The Labor Charter sees the nation realized in the Fascist State, and Schneider says the Ministry of Corporations is to control the whole economic life, though he calls that impossible in practice.

traditional-family.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno holds that mothers should work primarily in the home and that the father's wage must support the family.

unions-good.rationale: The Labor Charter makes the recognised syndicate the representative of workers and charges it with relief and training (arts. 3, 29-30), and Quadragesimo Anno welcomes workers' associations; both accept only unions under the corporative order.

unions-run-economy.rationale: The syndicates were controlled by the Ministry of Corporations, which also headed the corporations and had final authority (s7, s5).

voluntary-union-payments-at-work.rationale: Syndical dues were compulsory for everyone represented, members or not (s7), and the recognised syndicate may impose contributions on the whole group (art. 3, s9).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno speaks of an 'immense power and despotic economic dictatorship' consolidated in a few hands.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says the use of wealth must be brought within just distribution and criticises the concentration of wealth and power in a few hands.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Labor Charter leaves direction of the enterprise to the employer (art. 7); Quadragesimo Anno only advises modifying the wage contract so workers share in ownership, management or profits, and rejects the claim that all products belong to workers.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Labor Charter says direction of the enterprise is the right of the employer, who has the responsibility (art. 7).

summary: Corporate statism organises society into officially recognised occupational bodies, in Italy syndicates of employers and workers under a Ministry of Corporations and in Portugal sindicatos and grémios, that the state licenses, taxes and controls. Strikes are forbidden and disputes go to state arbitration; class collaboration replaces class conflict, and an authoritarian leader and a single party replace competitive parliamentary politics. Private ownership and private enterprise stay, but under state licensing, investment control and the national interest.
notes: Sources searched: Britannica on corporatism, Schmitter on state and societal corporatism, Schneider on Italy's corporative system, Gallagher on Salazar's New State, Quadragesimo Anno and the Labor Charter. Themes covered: labour and wages, property and enterprise, representation, the executive and parliament, strikes and unions, the family, religion, nation. Themes where the sources say nothing (most of world, ecology, technology, liberty beyond association, culture) stay null. Italy and Portugal differed; positions are recorded where the texts state them, not inferred from the regimes' character.
